paragraphs: A bag held in the hand hangs differently from one sitting on a table: the handles take the weight, the sides pull in, and the whole shape tells you roughly how full it is. That is why product photography for luggage is almost always shot being carried.
The model is light at 16,945 polygons and 17,285 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in blue, supplied in the carried pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits product and retail visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, travel and lifestyle advertising, character accessories and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A hare is not a large rabbit. It is born furred with its eyes open, lives above ground rather than in a burrow, and is built entirely around outrunning things: longer legs, longer ears, and a heart that takes up more of its chest than almost any other mammal's.
The model holds 36,934 polygons and 20,379 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. A furred build is offered separately.
At $89 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, documentary and education work, countryside scenes, game creatures, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A gear locker on wheels exists because turnout kit has to be somewhere specific at all times. Every set hangs in the same place, dries in the same place and is grabbed in the same order, and a station that gets that wrong loses seconds it cannot afford.
The model holds 323,151 polygons and 338,662 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the locker together with the gear. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits emergency services and station visualisation, equipment marketing, training material, interior scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2025.

A fire helmet is one of the few pieces of protective equipment with a national accent. The long rear brim of the American pattern exists to keep water off the neck, and it is so recognisable that it is used as a symbol of the profession worldwide.
The model holds 47,292 polygons and 49,641 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the head with the helmet. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $89 it suits emergency services visualisation, protective equipment marketing, character work, training material, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A field of maize at the dry stage is a wall of vertical lines. The leaves have gone papery, the stalks stand rigid, and the whole crop reads as texture rather than as individual plants, which is exactly the problem a modelled field has to solve.

This is by far the heaviest kind of asset in the library: 82,193,058 polygons and 92,516,453 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, because a convincing crop field means genuine plant geometry rather than cards. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits agricultural visualisation, landscape and environment scenes, documentary and education work, film backgrounds and high end architectural renders. On sale since 2026.

A forklift is deliberately unbalanced. The counterweight at the back is most of the machine's mass, the load hangs off the front, and the whole thing pivots on the front axle, which is why the rear wheels do the steering and why tipping one is so easy to do.

The model holds 445,942 polygons and 453,199 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 10 maps at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $89 it suits warehouse and logistics visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, industrial scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2015.

The tower stands on its own island in Bahrain Bay, and the void cut through its upper floors is the entire architectural gesture: a hole that frames sky, reduces wind load and makes the building identifiable from every approach to the city.
The model holds 281,628 polygons and 289,765 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits architectural and urban visualisation, hospitality and property presentation, tourism imagery, skyline scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The drive axle is where the engine's work finally reaches the road, and on a heavy truck it is a gearbox in its own right: a differential, hub reductions, and a housing that carries the entire weight of the load above it.
The model is built at subdivision level, 42,962 polygons and 46,690 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, so it holds up under close inspection. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $89 it suits automotive engineering visualisation, parts catalogues and technical material, manufacturing and aftermarket presentation, training and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A turret clock is a machine that has to be wound, regulated and repaired by somebody who climbs to it, and it was built to be understood by that person. Every wheel is exposed, every arbor reachable, and the going and striking trains sit side by side where they can be seen.
The model holds 254,971 polygons and 250,898 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the movement rather than the dial. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits museum and exhibition work, horological and engineering education, documentary and heritage material, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The holographic table is science fiction's favourite way to explain a plan. It exists because a briefing scene needs something for characters to stand around and point at, and a glowing model in mid air does that better than any screen ever could.
The scene holds 238,172 polygons and 249,356 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the table together with the projected spacecraft. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits science fiction film and animation, game environments, technology and concept presentation, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Every large building has a machine floor on top of it, and almost no render includes one. Chillers, ducts, fans and walkways: it is the least designed part of most architecture and the part that makes a rooftop look real rather than empty.
The scene holds 276,188 polygons and 317,231 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the plant and its supporting structure. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $89 it suits architectural and building services visualisation, engineering presentation, urban and rooftop scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A hooded desert scavenger is one of the most economical character designs there is: a robe, glowing points where the eyes should be, and nothing else visible. The viewer fills in everything under the cloth, which is why the silhouette works at any size.

The figure is light at 21,578 polygons and 22,158 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in an A pose ready for your own rig. It is built to CheckMate specification, and rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Cinema 4D and Maya.
At $89 it suits game characters, science fiction film and animation, concept art, fan illustration and previsualisation. On sale since 2025.

A forage wagon picks the crop up, chops it and carries it in one machine, which removes an entire vehicle from the harvest chain. On grass silage that matters enormously, because the whole operation is a race against the weather rather than against the calendar.
The model holds 526,955 polygons and 543,904 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout. It is built to CheckMate specification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $89 it suits agricultural machinery marketing, farming visualisation, rural scenes, training material, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The Labrador is the most owned dog in the world, and a white one with a muzzle fitted is a specific story: a working animal, a vet visit, or a jurisdiction with rules about it. The muzzle changes how the head reads more than any other accessory could.
The model holds 31,510 polygons and 31,494 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.

At $89 it suits pet and lifestyle visualisation, veterinary and animal welfare material, advertising, architectural and street scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
